key_insight: A.R.I.S. pairs a YOLOx-based real-time detector with a low-cost portable sorter to classify and separate metals, plastics, and circuit boards from shredded e-waste, enabling fast, accurate material identification at the point of processing.
problem_solved: Current recycling workflows lose recoverable materials because mixed shredded e-waste cannot be identified and separated quickly and affordably; A.R.I.S. addresses the need for accurate, low-latency sorting in constrained environments.
method: Low-cost, portable sorter hardware that processes shredded e-waste in a continuous pipeline.
YOLOx deep-learning model trained to detect and classify metals, plastics, and circuit boards with optimizations for low inference latency.
Integrated real-time pipeline (image capture → on-device inference → actuation) for immediate material routing.
impact: Demonstrates practical edge deployment of object-detection models for environmental applications, informing ML work on latency-aware model optimization, domain-specific datasets, and end-to-end system integration for sustainability use cases.
visual_elements: System schematic: camera + conveyor + sorter showing data flow from image capture to actuation
Side-by-side photo tiles or icons of the three target classes (metal, plastic, circuit board)
Performance panel: accuracy vs. latency summary (compact bar/arrow showing low latency and high accuracy)
Material recovery comparison: before vs. after sorting (stacked bars showing improved recovered mass or value)
paper_title: A.R.I.S.: Automated Recycling Identification System for E-Waste Classification Using Deep Learning
paper_authors: Dhruv Talwar, Harsh Desai, Wendong Yin, Goutam Mohanty, Rafael Reveles
